Q1: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are categorized with known significant hazards (Tier 1) for environmental impact and organ/systemic toxicity. Furthermore, expanded data indicate potential hazards (Tier 2) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive effects, and dermal/eye issues. While oral hazards are considered low to moderate (Tier 3), data regarding endocrine disruption and inhalation hazards are currently insufficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are on numerous lists of concern, most notably classified as Group 1 carcinogens by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) and identified as Persistent Organic Pollutants. They are also regulated under the Clean Water Act, EPA's Drinking Water Standard, and as Hazardous Air Pollutants, reflecting broad environmental and health concerns.
Q3: This chemical is very poorly characterized, evidenced by zero scientific literature references, an unspecified molecular formula, and its classification as a "Generic Registration" and "Manual Registration."
